title: The Catechism, again
tomorrow: can someone this competitive actually be holy?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the calendar: every day, someone, and all of them pointing back to Christ. Today, a big book with a small picture on it.
screen: `EVERY DAY, SOMEONE.` → `A BIG BOOK, A SMALL PICTURE.`

segments.voice: Band merch, team crests, the little icon on every app: a logo is supposed to tell you what's inside. So look at the logo on the Catechism of the Catholic Church, a thick book of what the Church teaches. It isn't a key, a seal or a gavel. It's a shepherd sitting under a tree, playing a set of pipes, with a sheep resting at his feet. Why put music on the cover of a book of doctrine?
screen: `A LOGO TELLS YOU WHAT'S INSIDE.` → `A SHEPHERD WITH PIPES.` → `MUSIC ON A BOOK OF DOCTRINE?`

segments.voice: The Catechism explains its own logo. The picture comes from an old Christian tombstone in the catacombs of Domitilla, in Rome. Christians used it for the rest and happiness of a soul with God. The book reads it like this: Christ the Good Shepherd leads his flock with his staff, draws them with the music of truth, the pipes, and lets them rest in the shade of the tree of life, which is his cross. So before you read a single line, the cover makes a claim: this book wants to be heard, like a voice you trust, not just looked up like a dictionary. Jesus says in John, in the Douay-Rheims Bible, "My sheep hear my voice." Inside, the music has four movements, the four pillars. The first is what Catholics believe, walked through the Creed. The second is how they celebrate, in the sacraments. The third is how they live, with the commandments. The fourth is how they pray, built around the Our Father. Here's the one to tell a friend: a book that big, full of doctrine and law, doesn't end on a rule. Its last part is about prayer, and its very last paragraph is about one word: Amen. Believe, celebrate, live, pray. The four hold each other up. Take one away and the others lean. Belief with no prayer goes dry; prayer with no life goes soft. That's why the shepherd plays one song, not four.
screen: `A TOMBSTONE IN THE CATACOMBS.` · `MY SHEEP HEAR MY VOICE.` · `BELIEVE, CELEBRATE, LIVE, PRAY.` · `THE LAST WORD IS AMEN.` · then, large: `FOUR PILLARS.`

segments.voice: Move slowly through the four with your body: a hand on your heart for believe, both hands open for celebrate, your feet pressed into the floor for live, palms together for pray. Then choose one pillar for this month, and keep that posture while the sit runs.
The Catechism. The Church's summary of its teaching, in four parts: believe, celebrate, live, pray.
Hold onto this: four pillars, and a shepherd's music running through all of them. That's today.

howItsDone: The Catechism of the Catholic Church is organized in four parts: the profession of faith, the celebration of the Christian mystery, life in Christ, and Christian prayer. Catholics use it for study, teaching and preparing for the sacraments.

options: Start with the four pillars: believe, celebrate, live, pray. Pick one to hold.
Memorize the whole Catechism before you go, and nothing up there can shake you.

chat.meaning: The Catechism maps faith in four parts that hold each other up. Holding one well is a real start; Mass alone or memorizing alone is only part of it.

Catechism.meaning: the Catholic Church's official summary of its teaching

catacombs.meaning: underground burial places of early Christians in Rome

Domitilla.meaning: an early Christian catacomb in Rome

Creed.meaning: the Church's summary statement of faith

sacraments.meaning: signs Catholics believe give grace, like baptism and the Eucharist
